_mrd.title: HRD Reader Experience and Reference Separation

content.outcome: Reshape the existing Governance and Work Management HRD publication families into prose-first human-readable specifications with explicit reader journeys and governed generated-reference separation, while preserving the full existing semantic contract.
preparation_boundary: Preparation created only the governed Change 010 inputs and GitHub issue 16.
The operator separately authorized complete implementation on 2026-08-26.
Implementation remains bounded by scope.json; Governance, Work Management, and Documentation Reference Standard MRDs remain protected and unchanged.
problem: Change 008 established distinct documentation output classes and Change 009 bound the Governance and Work Management specification families to that authority model, but several chapters still read as direct machine-record projections rather than reader-oriented specifications.
Lookup-heavy catalogs are embedded in specification chapters even when their primary purpose is exact reference, making conceptual flow harder to follow and increasing duplication across pages.
Normative rules are traceable, but some chapters present requirements as isolated rendered statements with too little explanatory context before or around them.
Navigation currently points mainly to the root specification and index; it does not fully express a progressive reader journey or reduce repeated explanation between related chapters.
The next improvement must change information architecture and rendering only, not Governance or Work Management semantics.

authority_model: Governance MRDs remain the sole owners of Governance semantics and normative requirements.
Work Management MRDs remain the sole owners of Work Management semantics and normative requirements.
KIS-DOC-CON-POL-001 controls documentation output classes and source authority boundaries.
KIS-DOC-SEM-REG-001 controls admitted documentation-reference roles and bounded permitted uses.
A human_readable_specification explains adopted normative behavior while preserving requirement strength, identifiers, ownership, and traceability.
A generated_reference exposes exact lookup-heavy facts from canonical sources without becoming a second owner.
MCP 2026 may guide specification structure and normative presentation only within the bounded roles already adopted; it cannot create KIS-specific semantics.
Google Developer Documentation guidance may improve prose, headings, lists, tables, and cross-references but cannot define KIS behavior.
External implementation references remain non-normative and cannot populate or override canonical KIS facts.
design_decisions: D1: Treat reader quality as publication architecture, not domain redesign. No Governance or Work Management fact may change merely to make prose easier to read.
D2: Use the existing Documentation Reference Standard output classes rather than inventing a new document taxonomy.

D3: Human-readable specification pages should explain concepts and operating models before exhaustive lookup detail, with normative statements embedded naturally where possible while preserving exact strength and stable identifiers.
D4: Generated-reference separation is selective, not automatic. A table stays in the specification when it is necessary to understand the normative model.
D5: Every moved fact must retain one canonical owner and deterministic traceability from specification to generated reference to source.
D6: Replace duplicate explanatory content with cross-reference when one chapter already owns the concept; duplicate exact data is allowed only when explicitly justified and consistency-verified.
D7: Navigation should express an intentional reader journey with bounded previous, next, and related links rather than a generic link hub.
D8: Diagrams are permitted only when they materially clarify lifecycle, authority, dependency, or handoff relationships and every diagram fact is source-derived.
D9: Semantic-equivalence and coverage tests are a hard gate: no existing rule may disappear, weaken, change owner, change enforcement binding, or acquire invented meaning.
D10: The implementation should establish reusable renderer patterns so later human_documentation work can inherit the reader-quality discipline without coupling task docs to specification structure.

requirements: R1: Change 010 implementation MUST NOT change Governance or Work Management domain semantics solely for reader-experience or presentation purposes.

R2: Every existing Governance and Work Management normative requirement MUST remain represented with the same stable rule ID, normative strength, canonical owner, and enforcement binding after restructuring.
R3: Human-readable specification pages MUST explain the relevant concept or operating model before presenting dense normative or lookup-heavy reference detail where doing so improves comprehension.
R4: Normative requirements MAY be embedded in explanatory prose, but generated wording MUST preserve the source requirement's meaning and MUST NOT weaken, strengthen, or invent obligations.

R5: Exact lookup-heavy facts MAY move from a human_readable_specification to generated_reference only when the reference derives from the same canonical owner and the specification retains sufficient explanation and deterministic linkage.
R6: Generated-reference separation MUST use the output classes already governed by KIS-DOC-CON-POL-001 and MUST NOT introduce a parallel documentation authority model.
R7: Specification-to-reference links MUST be deterministic, repository-portable, and verified for resolution.
R8: A moved fact MUST NOT be independently restated as new authority in the specification, reference page, manifest, or navigation metadata.
R9: The Governance publication MUST preserve the declared reader journey from overview through validation and enforcement.
R10: The Work Management publication MUST preserve the declared reader journey from domain model through conformance.
R11: Navigation SHOULD provide bounded previous, next, and related links where they materially help the declared reader journey; navigation MUST NOT obscure source and authority information.
R12: Cross-page duplication SHOULD be removed when one chapter already owns the explanation; a dependent chapter SHOULD link to that owner and focus on its distinct concern.
R13: Duplicate exact data MAY remain in more than one generated surface only when an explicit publication requirement justifies it and deterministic verification proves the copies agree.
R14: The 47-type Governance applicability catalog MUST remain completely available to readers even if moved to generated reference.
R15: The Governance relationship vocabulary and validation reason-code catalog MUST remain completely available and source-traceable even if their presentation location changes.

R16: The complete Work Management field catalog, controlled vocabularies, Project schema, Project views, bindings, feature modes, gates, and other currently published exact configuration facts MUST remain available and source-traceable after any reference separation.

R17: Work lifecycle transitions MUST have one primary human-readable explanation; provider-boundary documentation MUST reference that lifecycle instead of presenting an independently maintained semantic copy.
R18: Any generated diagram MUST derive every governed node, label, state, relationship, and edge from canonical sources and MUST participate in deterministic generation and stale/tamper detection.
R19: Generated diagrams MUST be supplemental explanatory projections and MUST NOT become normative authority or replace required text/table accessibility where exact values are needed.
R20: MCP 2026 and Google Developer Documentation guidance MUST remain within the source roles already governed by Change 008 and MUST NOT be used to rewrite KIS terminology or semantics.
R21: External implementation references and inferred evidence MUST NOT define the target information architecture unless a separately governed adoption decision promotes a bounded pattern.
R22: Publication manifests MUST bind all canonical inputs used by both human-readable specification and generated-reference outputs introduced or changed by the implementation.

R23: Automated tests MUST prove semantic preservation, complete fact/rule coverage, deterministic generation, link integrity, authority separation, and stale/tamper detection across both output classes.

R24: Human review MUST assess every regenerated page for reader journey, concept explanation, normative context, table/reference placement, navigation, duplication, terminology, source clarity, and authority separation before acceptance.

R25: The implementation MUST remain bounded to the future implementation scope approved after this preparation and MUST NOT broaden into human task/concept documentation, domain redesign, or general site redesign.

V2: A pre/post published-fact inventory proves every exact fact intentionally exposed before Change 010 remains available either in the specification or a deterministically linked generated-reference surface.
V3: Direct diffs under mrd/governance/** and mrd/work-management/** are empty for the reader-experience implementation unless a separately approved semantic change is raised outside Change 010.
V4: Tests prove generated-reference content can only be populated from canonical KIS facts or explicitly applicable normative protocol facts allowed by KIS-DOC-CON-POL-001.
V5: Tests prove MCP/Google/implementation-reference source roles cannot alter Governance or Work Management facts during prose or information-architecture generation.
V6: Every specification-to-reference and navigation link resolves in the generated corpus and remains repository-portable.
V7: Any retained duplicated exact data is generated from one canonical source path and a negative fixture proves divergence is detected.
V8: Any diagrams regenerate deterministically from canonical inputs; changing a relevant canonical input without regeneration causes verification to fail.

V11: Existing Governance and Work Management semantic/conformance tests remain green without weakened assertions.

future_acceptance: Governance and Work Management HRDs are recognizably human-readable specifications rather than machine-record dumps, while preserving all governed semantics.
Specification prose explains concepts before dense detail where appropriate and retains clear normative language without invented interpretation.
Lookup-heavy material is separated into generated reference only where doing so improves reading flow; readers can still reach every exact fact deterministically.
The Governance and Work Management reader journeys are explicit in page ordering and navigation.
Cross-page duplication is reduced, particularly Work Management field-authority and lifecycle repetition, without removing required conformance evidence.

The 47-type catalog, relationship vocabulary, validation reason codes, Work field catalog, controlled vocabularies, Project schema/views/bindings/features/gates, and other exact published facts remain complete and source-traceable.
Any diagrams are source-derived explanatory views with deterministic verification and no write-back authority.
MCP 2026 and Google guidance improve presentation only within their governed roles; KIS terminology and semantics remain KIS-owned.
Semantic-equivalence, coverage, link, deterministic-generation, stale/tamper, and authority-separation tests pass, and canonical verification succeeds on the exact implementation commit.
Page-by-page human review finds no material reader-flow, duplication, authority, or terminology defects.

risks: Semantic drift through prose: a well-intentioned rewrite could change requirement meaning even when rule IDs remain present.
Reference fragmentation: moving too much detail out of the specification could force readers to jump constantly between pages.
Hidden information loss: a table moved or removed for readability could accidentally drop a field, vocabulary value, reason code, or configuration fact.
Authority inversion: generated reference pages or diagrams can look authoritative unless ownership and source statements remain explicit.
Duplication drift: keeping exact data in multiple surfaces can create inconsistent generated copies if they are not driven from one source and verified.
Over-styling: following external presentation examples too closely could replace KIS terminology or structure with source-specific conventions.
Diagram maintenance: diagrams can become another stale projection unless every element is deterministic and verified.
Scope expansion: reader-quality work could drift into task documentation, website design, domain redesign, or a general publication-kernel refactor.
out_of_scope_for_preparation: Any change to Governance, Work Management, or Documentation Reference Standard MRDs or governed semantics.
Any renderer, publication profile, generated HRD, generated-reference, manifest, diagram, contract, test, script, verifier, or evidence implementation.

Any parent KIS change, GitHub Project schema change, MCP/FastMCP runtime change, external reference refresh, or reference-corpus modification.
Any pull request, merge, release, or implementation commit during this preparation-only step.
